My man and the kids are mostly away working in town, so I manage these 4.1 mu myself. Same ground I've always worked — wheat in winter, maize in summer, back and forth.

For the wheat, I plant in October after the maize comes off. I don't mess with the seed — I use the improved wheat my neighbor Old Wang gets from the dealer in town, same one most folks on our lane plant. It does well enough. I sow maybe a little thick, around a bag for the whole plot, because the cold can thin it out.

Before I sow I spread compound fertilizer — two bags (that's 100 jin) per mu, the 15-15-15 kind from the township shop. That's what my mother-in-law always did, that's what the neighbors do. Then around Qingming when the wheat stands up, I put urea, maybe half a bag per mu, about 20 jin. I'd rather put a little extra than see the leaves yellow and lose grain. Losing grain is real money; a bit more fertilizer is just a few yuan.

I water the wheat from the well — once before winter so it doesn't freeze dry, once at jointing, once when the head is filling. Three times is enough if the spring rain comes; four if it's dry. I spray once for the aphids when I see them on the heads, sometimes twice if they're bad.

For the maize I plant right after wheat harvest in June, no plowing — just drill it in, that's how everyone does it now with the machine service. The seed is the Zhengdan or whatever hybrid the dealer pushes that year; neighbors had good ears last year so I'll buy the same. Two bags of compound at planting, then urea at knee-high, about 30 jin per mu — maize eats more than wheat, I can tell from the leaves. Water once or twice if July is dry. Spray once for the borer when I see the little holes in the leaves.

Wheat usually gives me about 400 kg a mu if the weather is fair, maize a bit more, maybe 550. That's what I got most years.
